supply_chain_regulations.title: Subject Matter and Scope
supply_chain_regulations.description: Establishes the EU Cyber Resilience Act's scope covering products with digital elements placed on the EU market. The regulation applies to hardware and software products that can connect to a device or network, setting cybersecurity requirements for the entire product lifecycle from design through end-of-support. It excludes medical devices, vehicles, aviation, and products already covered by sector-specific EU legislation.
requirements: Products with digital elements must meet essential cybersecurity requirements
Covers both standalone software and embedded software in hardware
Applies to commercial and open source software with commercial activity
Remote data processing essential to product functionality is in scope
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements placed on the EU market, including software, IoT devices, and connected hardware. Excludes SaaS (unless essential for product function), medical devices, motor vehicles, and aviation products.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities in each Member State. Essential cybersecurity requirements apply from 2027-12-11.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Definitions
supply_chain_regulations.description: Defines key terms used throughout the regulation. A 'product with digital elements' means any software or hardware product and its remote data processing solutions that involve a direct or indirect connection to a device or network. 'Software bill of materials' (SBOM) is defined as a formal record of the components and supply chain relationships used to build software. Critical definitions also cover 'vulnerability', 'actively exploited vulnerability', and 'manufacturer'.
requirements: Products with digital elements include connected hardware and standalone software
SBOM must document components and supply chain relationships
Vulnerability defined as a weakness that can be exploited for security impact
Manufacturer includes legal persons who develop or have products developed under their name
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All entities subject to the CRA. Definitions apply across the entire regulation.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Definitions are interpretive and enforceable through the substantive articles they support.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Essential Cybersecurity Requirements
supply_chain_regulations.description: Products with digital elements may only be placed on the market if they meet the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Annex I when properly installed, maintained, and used for their intended purpose. The requirements cover both the security properties of the product itself (Part I) and the vulnerability handling processes of the manufacturer (Part II). Products must be designed and developed with an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on risk assessment.
requirements: Products must meet Annex I Part I security properties
Products must meet Annex I Part II vulnerability handling requirements
Security level must be proportionate to the risk
Products must be delivered with a secure-by-default configuration
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements placed on the EU market. Critical products (Annex III) face additional requirements.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Non-compliance may result in withdrawal from the market, fines up to EUR 15 million or 2.5% of worldwide turnover.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Important and Critical Products with Digital Elements
supply_chain_regulations.description: Classifies products into two risk categories: important products (Annex III) and critical products (Annex IV). Important products are divided into Class I (e.g., identity management systems, VPNs, SIEM, boot managers) and Class II (e.g., operating systems, firewalls, HSMs, smartcard readers). Critical products face the strictest conformity assessment requirements, potentially requiring third-party certification.
requirements: Class I important products may use harmonized standards or EU common specifications for conformity
Class II important products must involve a notified body or use a European cybersecurity certification scheme
Critical products (Annex IV) require European cybersecurity certification where available
Commission can update product classifications through delegated acts
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: Products listed in Annex III (important) and Annex IV (critical). Default products not in these annexes can self-assess compliance.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Notified bodies and market surveillance authorities. Higher scrutiny for Class II and critical products.
supply_chain_regulations.keywords: classification,important products,critical products,class i,class ii,risk categories,conformity

supply_chain_regulations.title: Obligations of Manufacturers
supply_chain_regulations.description: The central obligations article imposing comprehensive requirements on manufacturers. Manufacturers must perform cybersecurity risk assessments, integrate security throughout the product lifecycle, implement vulnerability handling, provide security updates for the support period, and document technical specifications. This article operationalizes the essential requirements from Annex I into concrete manufacturer obligations.
requirements: Conduct cybersecurity risk assessment before placing product on market
Design and develop product in accordance with essential requirements (Annex I)
Perform due diligence on third-party components integrated into the product
Identify and document vulnerabilities and components, including SBOM
Apply CE marking only when essential requirements are met
Provide security updates free of charge for the support period
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements placed on the EU market.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Fines up to EUR 15 million or 2.5% of worldwide turnover for non-compliance.

supply_chain_regulations.title: SBOM Obligation for Manufacturers
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must identify and document vulnerabilities and components contained in their products, including by drawing up an SBOM in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at minimum the top-level dependencies of the product. The SBOM must be generated and maintained throughout the product support period, enabling downstream vulnerability tracking and supply chain transparency.
requirements: Generate SBOM in machine-readable format
Include at minimum top-level dependencies
Use commonly accepted formats (SPDX, CycloneDX)
Maintain SBOM throughout the product support period
Make SBOM available to market surveillance authorities upon request
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements. SBOM must be available upon request by market surveillance authorities.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities can request SBOM. Non-provision may result in enforcement actions.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Technical Documentation Retention
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must keep technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for at least 10 years after the product is placed on the market, or for the duration of the support period, whichever is longer. This includes SBOMs, risk assessments, test reports, and vulnerability handling documentation. The retention period ensures regulatory authorities can audit compliance long after product release.
requirements: Retain technical documentation for minimum 10 years
Documentation includes EU declaration of conformity
Risk assessment results must be preserved
SBOM and vulnerability handling records must be maintained
Documentation must be made available to market surveillance authorities upon request
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities may request documentation at any time during the retention period.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Reporting Obligations
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must notify ENISA of any actively exploited vulnerability in their products and of any severe incident impacting product security. The notification must be submitted within 24 hours of awareness (early warning), with a full vulnerability notification within 72 hours, and a final report within 14 days. This creates an EU-wide vulnerability reporting regime similar to but distinct from NIS2 incident reporting.
requirements: Notify ENISA within 24 hours of awareness of actively exploited vulnerability (early warning)
Submit vulnerability notification within 72 hours with technical details
Provide final report within 14 days including mitigation measures
Notify affected users without undue delay and inform them of corrective measures
Report severe security incidents that impact product integrity
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements. Applies from September 2026 (earlier than full CRA).
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: ENISA coordinates notifications. Fines up to EUR 10 million or 2% of worldwide turnover for failure to report.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Obligations of Importers
supply_chain_regulations.description: Importers must verify that manufacturers have carried out conformity assessment, prepared technical documentation, affixed CE marking, and provided required information and instructions. Importers become responsible for ensuring that products they bring into the EU market comply with essential cybersecurity requirements. If an importer has reason to believe a product is non-compliant, they must not place it on the market and must inform the manufacturer and market surveillance authorities.
requirements: Verify manufacturer conformity assessment is complete
Ensure CE marking is properly affixed
Verify technical documentation (including SBOM) is available
Indicate importer name, trade name, and contact information on the product
Ensure storage and transport conditions do not compromise product compliance
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All importers of products with digital elements into the EU market.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Importers face same penalty regime as manufacturers for non-compliance.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Obligations of Distributors
supply_chain_regulations.description: Distributors must verify that the product bears CE marking, the manufacturer and importer have met their obligations (identification labeling, EU declaration of conformity, instructions), and the product is accompanied by required documentation. Distributors serve as an additional checkpoint in the supply chain, ensuring that non-compliant products do not reach end users.
requirements: Verify CE marking is present before making product available
Verify manufacturer and importer identification on the product
Ensure EU declaration of conformity accompanies the product
Report non-compliant products to market surveillance authorities
Cooperate with market surveillance authorities when requested
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All distributors of products with digital elements within the EU market.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Distributors face penalties for distributing products they know to be non-compliant.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Open Source Software Stewards
supply_chain_regulations.description: Introduces a new category for open source software foundations and maintainers who facilitate commercial use of open source products with digital elements. Open source stewards must establish and document a cybersecurity policy, cooperate with market surveillance authorities, and report actively exploited vulnerabilities. They face lighter obligations than manufacturers, recognizing the unique nature of open source development.
requirements: Establish and document a cybersecurity policy for secure development
Cooperate with market surveillance authorities
Report actively exploited vulnerabilities to ENISA
Facilitate vulnerability handling by downstream users
Provide a contact address for vulnerability reports
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: Legal persons (typically foundations like Apache, Eclipse, Linux Foundation) that facilitate development and commercial use of open source products with digital elements.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Lighter penalty regime than manufacturers: fines up to EUR 1 million. No conformity assessment or CE marking required.

supply_chain_regulations.title: EU Declaration of Conformity
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must draw up an EU declaration of conformity stating that the essential cybersecurity requirements have been fulfilled. The declaration must follow the structure in Annex V, identify the product, the manufacturer, and the conformity assessment procedure applied. The declaration must be continuously updated and made available in the language required by the Member State where the product is placed on the market.
requirements: Follow the structure specified in Annex V
Include product identification with unique identifier
State the conformity assessment procedure applied
Include reference to harmonized standards or common specifications used
Keep the declaration updated throughout the product lifecycle
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements placed on the EU market.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Missing or incomplete declaration is a compliance violation.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Conformity Assessment Procedures
supply_chain_regulations.description: Defines the conformity assessment procedures available for different product categories. Default (non-critical) products can use self-assessment (Module A). Important Class I products use harmonized standards with self-assessment or Module B+C with a notified body. Important Class II and critical products require notified body involvement (Module B+C or Module H). This graduated approach reflects the risk-based nature of the regulation.
requirements: Default products: self-assessment using internal control (Module A)
Class I important products: Module A with harmonized standards, or Module B+C with notified body
Class II important products: Module B+C or Module H with notified body
Critical products: Module B+C or Module H, or European cybersecurity certification scheme
Conformity assessment must cover both product security and vulnerability handling
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements, with procedure requirements varying by product classification.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Notified bodies and market surveillance authorities oversee conformity assessment. Incorrect procedure is a compliance violation.
supply_chain_regulations.keywords: conformity assessment,module a,module b,module c,module h,notified body,self-assessment

supply_chain_regulations.title: Notified Bodies
supply_chain_regulations.description: Establishes the framework for notified bodies that conduct third-party conformity assessments for important and critical products. Notified bodies must be designated by Member States and meet competence, independence, and impartiality requirements. They must have demonstrated expertise in cybersecurity and product assessment. The notified body system mirrors existing EU product safety frameworks like CE marking for machinery.
requirements: Notified bodies must be designated by national notifying authorities
Must demonstrate cybersecurity competence and technical expertise
Must be independent and free from conflicts of interest
Must maintain adequate staffing and financial resources
Must have liability insurance for conformity assessment activities
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: Organizations seeking to become notified bodies for CRA conformity assessment, and manufacturers requiring third-party assessment.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: National notifying authorities designate and monitor notified bodies. Commission maintains a public registry (NANDO).

supply_chain_regulations.title: Market Surveillance
supply_chain_regulations.description: Member States must designate market surveillance authorities responsible for enforcing the CRA. These authorities have powers to request documentation (including SBOMs), conduct product evaluations, request corrective actions, order product withdrawal or recall, and impose fines. The market surveillance framework aligns with Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and product compliance.
requirements: Member States designate market surveillance authorities
Authorities can request technical documentation and SBOM
Authorities can conduct product cybersecurity evaluations
Authorities can order corrective measures, withdrawal, or recall
Cross-border cooperation between market surveillance authorities
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: National market surveillance authorities in all EU Member States.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: National market surveillance authorities with powers under Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Penalties
supply_chain_regulations.description: Establishes the penalty framework for CRA violations. Maximum fines are structured in three tiers based on severity: EUR 15 million or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover for failing to meet essential cybersecurity requirements; EUR 10 million or 2% for other obligation violations; EUR 5 million or 1% for providing incorrect or incomplete information. Member States may apply additional penalties. Micro and small enterprises receive proportionate penalties.
requirements: Essential requirement violations: up to EUR 15 million or 2.5% of worldwide turnover
Other obligation violations: up to EUR 10 million or 2% of worldwide turnover
Incorrect information: up to EUR 5 million or 1% of worldwide turnover
Penalties must be effective, proportionate, and dissuasive
SME proportionality considerations apply
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All economic operators subject to the CRA: manufacturers, importers, distributors, and open source stewards (with lower caps).
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: National competent authorities impose penalties. Appeals through national judicial systems.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Security by Design and Default
supply_chain_regulations.description: Products must be designed, developed, and produced to ensure an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on risks. Products must be delivered with a secure-by-default configuration, including the absence of known exploitable vulnerabilities. The product must protect the confidentiality and integrity of stored, transmitted, and processed data. Products must be designed to limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces.
requirements: Design products to limit attack surfaces including external interfaces
Deliver products without known exploitable vulnerabilities
Apply secure-by-default configuration out of the box
Protect confidentiality and integrity of data at rest and in transit
Ensure availability and minimize negative impact on other devices/networks
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements (Annex I Part I applies universally).
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Assessed during conformity assessment. Market surveillance authorities can evaluate compliance.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Access Control and Authentication
supply_chain_regulations.description: Products must implement appropriate authentication, identity, and access management mechanisms. This includes protection against unauthorized access, secure authentication mechanisms proportionate to the risk, and the ability to manage and restrict access to functions and data. Multi-factor authentication should be supported where appropriate for the product's risk profile.
requirements: Implement access control mechanisms appropriate to the risk
Protect against unauthorized access through authentication
Support secure authentication proportionate to product risk
Ensure proper identity management for users and components
Enable management of access privileges and permissions
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements that involve user authentication or access control.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Assessed during conformity assessment.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Data Protection and Cryptography
supply_chain_regulations.description: Products must protect the confidentiality of data stored, processed, or transmitted using state-of-the-art cryptographic mechanisms. Data integrity must be ensured, and products must minimize data collection to what is necessary for the intended function. Encryption at rest and in transit must be implemented where appropriate, with key management following established best practices.
requirements: Use state-of-the-art encryption for data in transit and at rest
Implement proper cryptographic key management
Minimize data collection and processing to what is necessary
Protect data integrity against unauthorized modification
Support secure deletion of personal and sensitive data
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements that handle data storage, processing, or transmission.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Assessed during conformity assessment. Alignment with GDPR data protection principles.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Logging and Monitoring
supply_chain_regulations.description: Products must record security-relevant events and provide mechanisms for users to access and manage these logs. Logging should cover authentication events, configuration changes, and security-relevant activities. The logging mechanism must protect log integrity and support incident detection and forensic analysis while respecting data protection requirements.
requirements: Record security-relevant events including authentication and configuration changes
Provide user access to security logs
Protect log integrity against tampering
Support audit and forensic analysis capabilities
Balance logging with data protection and privacy requirements
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements, proportionate to the product's risk level and capabilities.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Assessed during conformity assessment.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Secure Update Mechanism
supply_chain_regulations.description: Products must support secure and timely updates to address vulnerabilities. The update mechanism must ensure the integrity and authenticity of updates through cryptographic verification. Automatic update capabilities should be provided where appropriate, with user notification and control. Updates must not degrade the product's existing security posture.
requirements: Implement secure update mechanism with integrity verification
Provide automatic update capability where appropriate
Notify users of available security updates
Ensure updates are authenticated and cannot be tampered with
Security updates must be provided free of charge
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements that can receive software updates.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Assessed during conformity assessment. Failure to provide security updates is an ongoing obligation.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Resilience and Availability
supply_chain_regulations.description: Products must be designed to ensure availability and continuity of essential functions, including resilience against denial-of-service attacks. Products should minimize the impact of security incidents on other connected devices and networks. Where appropriate, products must support redundancy mechanisms and graceful degradation under adverse conditions.
requirements: Design for resilience against denial-of-service attacks
Minimize impact of security incidents on connected devices and networks
Support continuity of essential functions during incidents
Implement graceful degradation under adverse conditions
Ensure products do not adversely affect availability of other services
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements, particularly those connected to networks or other devices.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Assessed during conformity assessment.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Vulnerability Identification and Documentation
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must identify and document all known vulnerabilities in their products, including vulnerabilities in third-party components. This requires maintaining an SBOM and continuously monitoring vulnerability databases and advisories for components used in the product. Documented vulnerabilities must be assessed for impact and prioritized for remediation.
requirements: Identify vulnerabilities in proprietary and third-party components
Maintain SBOM for vulnerability tracking throughout product lifecycle
Monitor vulnerability databases (NVD, OSV, vendor advisories) continuously
Assess and prioritize vulnerabilities based on impact and exploitability
Document vulnerability status and remediation plans
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities can audit vulnerability handling processes.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Vulnerability Remediation and Updates
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must address and remediate identified vulnerabilities without undue delay through security updates. Security patches must be provided free of charge throughout the product support period. When a vulnerability cannot be immediately fixed, manufacturers must provide workarounds and communicate the residual risk to users. Regression testing must ensure updates do not introduce new vulnerabilities.
requirements: Remediate vulnerabilities without undue delay
Provide security updates free of charge
Communicate residual risk when immediate fix is not available
Perform regression testing on security updates
Ensure updates do not degrade product security or functionality
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements during the product support period.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Failure to provide timely updates may result in enforcement actions.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must establish a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy and provide a contact point for vulnerability reports. The policy must define the process for receiving, triaging, and responding to vulnerability reports from external researchers. Manufacturers must engage in good faith with vulnerability reporters and acknowledge reports within a reasonable timeframe.
requirements: Establish a public vulnerability disclosure policy
Provide a dedicated contact point for vulnerability reports (e.g., security.txt)
Define process for receiving, triaging, and responding to reports
Acknowledge vulnerability reports within a defined timeframe
Engage in good faith with security researchers
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. ISO 29147 and ISO 30111 provide implementation guidance.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Security Testing and Verification
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must regularly test and review the security of their products with digital elements. This includes both automated testing (SAST, DAST, fuzzing, SCA) and manual review. Testing must cover the product's own code and the integration of third-party components. Test results must be documented and used to drive security improvements.
requirements: Conduct regular security testing throughout product lifecycle
Apply static analysis (SAST) and dynamic analysis (DAST)
Test third-party component integration for security issues
Perform fuzzing and penetration testing where appropriate
Document test results and remediation actions
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Assessed during conformity assessment. Test results part of technical documentation.

framework_mappings.SSDF: PW.5 (Test executable code), PW.6 (Configure compilation/build), PW.7 (Review and audit)

supply_chain_regulations.title: Support Period and End-of-Life
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must determine and clearly communicate the expected product support period during which security updates will be provided. The support period must be proportionate to the expected product lifetime but must be at minimum 5 years. Manufacturers must inform users before the support period ends and provide guidance on secure decommissioning or migration to supported alternatives.
requirements: Define and communicate product support period (minimum 5 years)
Provide security updates throughout the support period
Notify users before end of support period
Provide decommissioning or migration guidance at end of life
Support period information must be included at point of sale
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Support period commitment is a binding obligation.
supply_chain_regulations.keywords: support period,end of life,eol,lifecycle,security updates,decommissioning,5 years

supply_chain_regulations.title: Information and Instructions for Users
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must provide users with essential information and instructions accompanying the product. This includes the manufacturer's identity and contact details, the product's intended purpose, a description of essential security features, known residual risks, the support period with end date, and instructions for secure installation, configuration, and decommissioning. The information must be in a language easily understood by users.
requirements: Provide manufacturer identity, contact, and single point of contact for vulnerability reports
Describe the product's intended purpose and cybersecurity features
Document known residual risks and recommended security configurations
State the support period end date and expected update frequency
Provide instructions for secure installation, configuration, operation, and disposal
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All products with digital elements placed on the EU market.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Missing information is a compliance violation.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Important Products - Class I
supply_chain_regulations.description: Lists Class I important products that require either self-assessment using harmonized standards or third-party conformity assessment. Class I includes: identity management systems, standalone and embedded browsers, password managers, malware detection software, VPNs, network management systems, SIEM tools, boot managers, public key infrastructure tools, digital certificate issuance software, physical and virtual network interfaces, operating systems not covered by Class II, routers and modems, and microprocessors.
requirements: Self-assessment if harmonized standards are applied fully
Third-party assessment (Module B+C) if harmonized standards are not applied
Compliance with all essential cybersecurity requirements (Annex I)
Technical documentation per Annex VII
EU declaration of conformity per Annex V
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: Products listed in Annex III Class I: identity management, browsers, password managers, antivirus, VPNs, SIEM, boot managers, PKI tools, network interfaces, routers, microprocessors, etc.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Notified bodies for third-party assessment.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Important Products - Class II
supply_chain_regulations.description: Lists Class II important products that require mandatory third-party conformity assessment by a notified body. Class II products face higher security scrutiny due to their critical role in system security. The list includes: hypervisors and container runtime systems, firewalls, tamper-resistant microprocessors, tamper-resistant microcontrollers, and hardware security modules (HSMs).
requirements: Mandatory third-party conformity assessment (Module B+C or Module H)
Assessment by a designated notified body
Compliance with all essential cybersecurity requirements (Annex I)
Technical documentation per Annex VII with third-party review
EU declaration of conformity per Annex V
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: Products listed in Annex III Class II: hypervisors, container runtimes, firewalls, tamper-resistant processors, HSMs.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Notified bodies conduct mandatory assessment. Market surveillance authorities enforce compliance.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Third-Party Component Due Diligence
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must exercise due diligence when integrating third-party components, including open source software, into their products. This includes verifying that third-party components do not compromise the product's compliance with essential cybersecurity requirements. Manufacturers must monitor the security status of integrated components and ensure timely patching when vulnerabilities are discovered in dependencies.
requirements: Exercise due diligence on all integrated third-party components
Verify that third-party components do not compromise product compliance
Monitor vulnerability databases for third-party component vulnerabilities
Maintain an up-to-date inventory (SBOM) of third-party components
Ensure timely patching when third-party vulnerabilities are discovered
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements that integrate third-party components (which includes virtually all software).
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities. Due diligence failure is a compliance violation.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Risk Assessment Documentation
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must include a cybersecurity risk assessment in the technical documentation required under Article 31. The risk assessment must analyze the cybersecurity risks associated with the product, identify applicable threats, and demonstrate how the essential requirements address those risks. The risk assessment must be updated when significant changes occur.
requirements: Conduct cybersecurity risk assessment before placing product on market
Document risk assessment in technical documentation
Identify applicable threats and attack vectors
Demonstrate how essential requirements address identified risks
Update risk assessment when significant changes occur to the product or threat landscape
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Risk assessment reviewed during conformity assessment. Market surveillance authorities may request it.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Free and Open Source Software
supply_chain_regulations.description: Clarifies that free and open source software not supplied in the course of a commercial activity is exempt from CRA obligations. However, open source software becomes subject to the regulation when it is supplied as part of a commercial activity, which includes monetization through support services, dual licensing, or integration into commercial products. This provision attempts to protect volunteer open source maintainers while ensuring commercial open source meets security standards.
requirements: Open source software supplied outside commercial activity is exempt
Commercial use of open source triggers CRA obligations
Monetization (support, dual licensing) constitutes commercial activity
Integration into commercial products makes open source in-scope
Voluntary financial contributions alone do not constitute commercial activity
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: Open source software developers and foundations. Determines whether CRA obligations apply based on commercial activity.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Market surveillance authorities determine whether commercial activity triggers CRA obligations.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Technical Documentation Requirements
supply_chain_regulations.description: Manufacturers must compile technical documentation before placing a product on the market. The documentation must contain all information necessary to demonstrate conformity with essential requirements, including: a general description of the product, design and development details, cybersecurity risk assessment, SBOM, EU declaration of conformity, applied harmonized standards, and the results of conformity assessment.
requirements: General description including intended purpose and essential features
Design and manufacturing documentation
Cybersecurity risk assessment results
SBOM documenting product components
List of harmonized standards or common specifications applied
Results of conformity assessment procedure
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All manufacturers of products with digital elements placed on the EU market.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Technical documentation must be available to market surveillance authorities upon request.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Voluntary Reporting and Information Sharing
supply_chain_regulations.description: Economic operators and other entities may voluntarily notify ENISA and national CSIRTs of vulnerabilities and cyber threats that are not subject to mandatory reporting. ENISA is encouraged to facilitate voluntary information sharing through platforms and tools. This complements the mandatory reporting under Article 11 by creating channels for broader threat intelligence sharing across the EU supply chain ecosystem.
requirements: Voluntary reporting channel available through ENISA single reporting platform
Reports can cover vulnerabilities not subject to mandatory reporting
Reports can cover near-miss incidents and cyber threats
ENISA forwards relevant information to affected Member State CSIRTs
Reporting entity identity can be kept confidential upon request
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All economic operators, CERTs, security researchers, and any entity with relevant vulnerability or threat information.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Voluntary -- no penalty for not reporting. ENISA coordinates the reporting platform.
